title: Pattern Headings: Animals
scope: Free-floating subdivisions for use under headings for individual animals and groups of animals at all taxonomic levels (common or scientific names), including wild and domestic animals, breeds, age and sex groups, and extinct and fossil animals; pattern headings Fishes and Cattle.
pattern_category: individual animals and groups of animals
general_notes: The headings covered by this pattern include headings for individual animals and groups of animals at all taxonomic levels, established using either common or scientific names, including animals in their natural or wild state, and those raised or cared for by humans. The pattern also covers headings for extinct and fossil animals.
Included are individual breeds or groups of domestic animals, for example, Tennessee walking horse; Poodles; and headings for age and sex groups, for example, Chicks; Foals; Cows.

The general headings Animals; Domestic animals; and Livestock are excluded from this category. The category also does not include individually named animals such as Seattle Slew (Race horse) or Morris (Cat).

The subdivisions below are also not used under phrase headings of the type [animal] as laboratory animals or [animal] as pets. Instead, these phrase headings are assigned along with headings of the type [animal]--[appropriate subdivision from the list below].

Also excluded are headings for individual microorganisms. If a subdivision from this list is needed for use under a heading for an individual microorganism, it is established editorially rather than assigned as a free-floating subdivision.
Establish subdivisions appropriate for animals in general under Fishes; establish subdivisions specific to domestic animals under Cattle.
Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.

Subdivisions on this list that represent specific pathological conditions, for example, --Abnormalities; --Fractures; --Infections; --Virus diseases; --Wounds and injuries, may be further subdivided by subdivisions listed under the subdivision --Diseases, for example, --Diseases--Diagnosis; --Diseases--Treatment.

LC practice: As stated in H 1075, Library of Congress catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. The form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by LC catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.
